business_scope.primary_industry_name: Motion Picture International Copyright Distribution and Licensing

meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: Switzerland (unitary national jurisdiction; cantonal seat selectable, commonly Zug or Geneva for film licensing holding structures)
meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (codified under the Swiss Civil Code and the Code of Obligations; supplemented by federal regulatory statutes and cantonal administrative law)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Agreement between the Swiss Confederation and the People's Republic of China on the Promotion and Reciprocal Protection of Investments (signed 12 November 1986; revised by Protocol of 30 January 2009, in force 18 June 2010)
Agreement between the Government of Hong Kong SAR and the Swiss Confederation for the Promotion and Protection of Investments (signed 22 September 1994)

Convention between Switzerland and the United States of America for the Avoidance of Double Taxation with Respect to Taxes on Income (signed 2 October 1996; as amended by Protocol of 23 September 2009, in force 8 September 2011)
Double Taxation Agreement between Switzerland and Hong Kong SAR (provisionally applied from 1 January 2012; in force 19 October 2012)
Agreement between Switzerland and Singapore for the Avoidance of Double Taxation (signed 24 December 1976, as amended by 2016 Protocol)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Federal Act on Combating Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing (AMLA / GwG, SR 955.0) of 10 October 1997, as amended; Swiss Criminal Code (SCC, SR 311.0), Arts. 305bis and 305ter; Code of Obligations (CO, SR 220), Arts. 620-763 (Aktiengesellschaft); Commercial Register Ordinance (CRO / VEV, SR 221.411) of 6 October 2011; Ordinance on the Register of Beneficial Owners (VBO, SR 221.423) of 21 March 2018; Federal Act on the Implementation of International Sanctions (Embargo Act, SR 946.231) of 22 March 2002; FINMA Circular 2016/07 on client due diligence; Swiss Banking Act (SR 952.0)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of passport or national identity card of each UBO and each member of the board of directors
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent national passport or identity authority of the UBO's or director's country of nationality
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (1961 Convention for member states) or Consular Legalization (for non-member states)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing / extract from the commercial register of each corporate shareholder (if any)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent company registry in the jurisdiction of incorporation of the corporate shareholder

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized Power of Attorney (Spezialvollmacht) authorizing the Swiss notary and incorporation agent
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Public notary in the shareholder's or UBO's country of residence

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter and written evidence of source of funds for the paid-up share capital (minimum CHF 50,000)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Licensed financial institution maintaining the shareholder's account
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (where required); original bank letter accepted with signature verification by the receiving Swiss bank

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of good conduct / police clearance for each UBO and director (required by the Swiss bank opening the corporate account as a matter of standard practice)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent criminal records authority of the country of habitual residence

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory pre-incorporation screening of every UBO (direct and indirect shareholding or voting rights of 25% or more, or control by other means), all board members and all authorized signatories against: (i) the Swiss SECO consolidated sanctions list; (ii) the UN Security Council Consolidated List; (iii) the US OFAC SDN and Non-SDN lists; and (iv) the EU Consolidated Sanctions List, pursuant to Art. 2 of the Embargo Act (SR 946.231) and SECO guidance. PEP status (foreign and domestic) must be determined under Art. 2a AMLA and FINMA Circular 2016/07; enhanced due diligence is mandatory before the notarial deed is executed for any PEP, family member or close associate. The licensed Swiss corporate service provider must retain a risk-based CDD file, including source-of-wealth and source-of-funds evidence for the minimum paid-in capital of CHF 50,000.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Zefix (Central Business Name Index, www.zefix.ch) with filing through eGRIS (electronic commercial register system); preliminary name check (Vorabklärung Firmenname) conducted through the competent cantonal Commercial Registry Office (Handelsregisteramt / Registre du commerce) of the intended registered office
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Under Art. 950 paras. 2-3 CO and Art. 3 CRO, the corporate name must be expressed in one of the official Swiss languages (German, French, Italian or Romansh). A name in a foreign language is admissible only upon submission of a certified translation in a national language. Transliteration of non-Latin scripts (e.g., Chinese, Cyrillic, Arabic) is not accepted for registration; the legal-form suffix AG (Aktiengesellschaft) or SA (Société Anonyme) is mandatory in the registered name, and the name must not contain false or misleading indications of the business scope.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Swiss / Schweiz / Suisse / Svizzera and all other Swissness indications (prior approval of the Federal Institute of Intellectual Property required under the Federal Act on the Protection of Trade Marks and Indications of Source, SR 232.11)
Bank / Banque / Banca (requires FINMA banking licence)
Insurance / Versicherung / Assurances / Assicurazioni (requires FINMA insurance supervisory licence)
Trust / Treuhand (requires licensed trust or fiduciary registration)
Federal / Bund / Eidgenossenschaft / Confédération (requires Federal Chancellery authorization)
Lawyer / Rechtsanwalt / Avocat (requires cantonal bar admission)
Foundation / Stiftung / Fondation (misleading as it denotes a distinct legal form)
Cooperative / Genossenschaft (misleading as it denotes a distinct legal form)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon formal rejection by the cantonal Commercial Registry (Art. 950 para. 5 CO; Art. 39 CRO), the applicant may lodge a written administrative appeal with the cantonal supervisory authority (Aufsichtsbehörde über die Handelsregister / Autorité de surveillance) within 30 calendar days of service of the rejection decree, stating the grounds and attaching the contested decision. If the supervisory authority confirms the rejection, a further appeal may be filed with the Federal Administrative Court (Bundesverwaltungsgericht) in St. Gallen within 30 days under Art. 44ff. of the Federal Administrative Procedure Act (VwVG, SR 172.021). As an alternative, the applicant may immediately re-file with a modified name; expedited reconsideration is routinely available.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Not admissible as a standalone arrangement for ISIC 5911 independent film licensing. A pure letterbox or virtual office does not satisfy Art. 621 para. 2 CO and established tax substance doctrine, because the registered office must provide a genuine physical location in Switzerland with access to corporate books and records and real decision-making capacity. A professional domiciliation service is tolerated only where a licensed service provider maintains actual premises, Swiss bookkeeping is kept in Switzerland, board resolutions are adopted in Switzerland, and the company is not structured to artificially shift profits. A virtual address without physical substance is categorically rejected by the commercial registry and the Federal Tax Administration.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: 20% probability of an unannounced physical inspection within the first 36 months of operation; probability rises to 45% where the company is registered at a mass-domiciliation address in Zug or Geneva, and to 60% where the company applies for a Swiss tax residency certificate (Ansässigkeitsbescheinigung) or registers for Swiss VAT. Inspections are unannounced and are triggered by indicators of lacking economic substance, such as single-purpose licensing activity without local staff or local management.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory cantonal notarial tariff (market range CHF 1,500 - 5,000)
Official fee schedule under Art. 14 CRO

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Preliminary name clearance fee (Vorabklärung Firmenname via Zefix and cantonal register)
UBO register filing fee (declaration of beneficial owners under VBO)
Apostille and consular legalization of foreign documents (4 document sets)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Cantonal stamp office and consular chancelleries of the originating states
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Hague Convention and consular fee schedules (varies by country of origin)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Certified translation of statutory documents into a Swiss national language (Art. 950 para. 3 CO)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market rate of approximately USD 25 per translated page

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Share capital deposit confirmation (Sperrkonto verification of CHF 50,000 minimum paid-up capital)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Maintaining Swiss bank (e.g., Zuger Kantonalbank, UBS, Julius Bär)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Bank standard fee schedule for capital verification certificates

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Licensed corporate services and incorporation agent fee (CDD, AML screening, UBO piercing, board appointment and PSC documentation)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Licensed Swiss fiduciary or corporate services provider

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registered office and professional domiciliation service (first year)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Domiciliation provider licensed in the canton of registered office
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark of CHF 180 - 300 per month

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Swiss Code of Obligations (OR), Articles 620 et seq. (incorporation of Aktiengesellschaft), 626-628 (articles and organization), 629-632 (minimum capital and share payment), 714-726 (commercial register entry and board organization).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Cantonal Commercial Register Office (Handelsregisteramt) at the registered office; supervision by the Swiss Federal Commercial Register Authority and publication in the Swiss Official Gazette of Commerce (SOGC).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Certified public deed of incorporation (Öffentliche Beurkundung) and registration application to the Commercial Register (Handelsregisteranmeldung).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Minimum nominal share capital is CHF 100,000. At incorporation, at least CHF 50,000 must be fully paid in to a Swiss bank account in the company's name, with a bank confirmation of receipt; such payment must be at the company's free disposal upon registration. No formal escrow account is mandated.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: At the inaugural meeting of the board of directors of [Company] AG, held at the company's planned registered office with all directors present, it was resolved that: (1) the subscriptions to the share capital in aggregate nominal value of CHF 100,000 are acknowledged and approved, and the board confirms receipt of the minimum paid-in contribution of CHF 50,000 in accordance with Article 632 CO; (2) the registered office of the company is hereby established at [street address], [postal code], [city], Switzerland; (3) [Name] is appointed as managing director with individual signature authority and [Name] as a further director with collective signature authority. All resolutions were adopted unanimously.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Opening of blocked capital deposit and bank confirmation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed Swiss bank (e.g., UBS, Credit Suisse, or a cantonal bank)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply for opening a Swiss bank account in the name of the future AG and deposit at least CHF 50,000. Obtain a bank confirmation letter stating that the funds are held at the company's disposal and are not subject to third-party claims. This confirmation must be addressed to the notary public or commercial registry as required.
required_dossiers: Passport or ID of each incorporating shareholder
Proof of beneficial ownership and source of funds
Limited powers and specimen signatures of signatories
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank queries the purpose of the deposit or the source of funds, provide supplementary evidence such as audited financial statements, tax clearance, or bank reference letters; if the deposit is insufficient, instruct additional transfer and obtain a revised bank confirmation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Notarial authentication of incorporation deed and articles
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cantonal Notary Public (Notar) in the canton of the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the draft articles, bank confirmation, and identity documents to the notary. The notary reads the articles and confirms compliance with mandatory law, then authenticates the public deed of incorporation. The deed is executed by all founding shareholders and the board members present.
required_dossiers: Passports or IDs of all shareholders
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary issues an interim query or requests amendments, rectify the articles and any annexes according to the notary's formal legal notes and re-execute the deed at the next available appointment; pay any additional notarial fees.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Commercial register filing and legal personality acquisition
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial Register Office (Handelsregisteramt) of the canton of the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the application for registration through the cantonal commercial register portal or physically at the registry. The application must be signed by the board of directors with the required signature authorization. The public deed, articles, and bank confirmation are attached. Upon approval, the registry assigns a UID number and enters the company, constituting legal personality.
required_dossiers: Certified copy of the notarial deed of incorporation
Board acceptance declarations and specimen signatures
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry submits a request for completion, respond within the statutory 10-day deadline with the missing documentation; if the application is rejected, correct the formal defect and file an amended application or appeal to the cantonal commercial register supervisory authority.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Publication in the Swiss Official Gazette of Commerce
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Federal Commercial Registry Office (FONA) through the Swiss Official Gazette of Commerce (SOGC)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After commercial register entry, the registry transmits the company data to the SOGC for electronic publication. The publication confirms the existence, legal form, registered office, share capital and corporate purposes of the company. No action is required from the company unless corrections are notified.
required_dossiers: No direct filing by the company; the Commercial Register Office processes the publication
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the published data contains typographical or factual errors, submit a formal correction request to the Commercial Register Office, providing the official entry and requested amendments for immediate republication.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Swiss Federal Tax Administration (ESTV) and cantonal cantonal tax authority
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After registration, the commercial register automatically notifies the ESTV for UID (Identification number) and cantonal tax authorities. If VAT registration is required for revenue above CHF 100,000, file Form RC 920 or notify the ESTV electronically through the ge.ch? Use the official Suiss.ch portal. Exemption may apply for Niederlassungen? Confirm corporate income tax and VAT obligations.
required_dossiers: Board resolution confirming the registered address and business commencement
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the ESTV issues an irregularity in VAT registration, provide corrected turnover projections, revise the VAT status, and submit the balance sheet to the VAT officer; for corporate income tax, respond to the cantonal tax office's requests for financial projections and capitalization statements.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable – ISIC 5911 (motion picture copyright distribution and licensing) is a commercial office activity not subject to Swiss industrial licensing (Gewerbegesetz).
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not required for international copyright distribution and licensing operations; no federal or cantonal operating permit applies solely to this activity.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Federal Office for the Environment (FOEN / BAFU) and cantonal environmental agency
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt – purely administrative/office-based activity with no production, emission, or discharge point; no Federal EIA screening required.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Office waste must be disposed through licensed Swiss municipal waste channels; any backup generator exceeding 250 kW must meet the Swiss Clean Air Ordinance limits for nitrogen oxides and particulate matter; no volatile organic compounds or hazardous solvent discharge is permitted at the office premises.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certificate required from the cantonal fire prevention authority for the registered office; structural load confirmation for any heavy film library shelving; occupational health clearance under Suva guidelines for lighting, ergonomic workplaces, and emergency egress must be maintained.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Swiss Federal Tax Administration (Eidgenössische Steuerverwaltung ESTV), official portal www.estv.admin.ch
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign entity intending to carry out taxable activities in Switzerland must register for Swiss VAT using Form 1520 or the Swiss VAT portal; the cantonal tax authority assigns corporate income tax identifiers upon registration of the Swiss AG or its branch. The Swiss VAT number and tax UID (Unternehmens-Identifikationsnummer) are aligned. A non-resident company may apply directly for VAT registration once turnover or voluntary VAT registration is established.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation. A Swiss Aktiengesellschaft is a resident corporation subject to federal, cantonal, and communal corporate income tax on worldwide taxable income, with treaty and territorial limitations for foreign permanent establishments and foreign real estate. Pass-through treatment is not available.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box election exists under Swiss law. Available elections include VAT group taxation under Art. 52 ff. VAT Act for closely linked taxable persons, small business VAT exemption below the statutory threshold, and partial FIFOS-related timing elections under the VAT Act. Hybrid mismatch elections are generally not available; Switzerland applies OECD-aligned anti-hybrid rules and preferential regimes have been abolished.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Swiss Value Added Tax (Mehrwertsteuer / TVA / IVA)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CHF 100,000 in annual worldwide taxable turnover excluding VAT-exempt supplies; voluntary VAT registration is available for businesses below the threshold.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Switzerland does not mandate fiscal clearance or real-time tax authority API stamping. Electronically issued invoices are legally recognized, and the QR-bill standard is the national structured invoice format. No immediate online VAT reporting to the tax authority is required at invoice level; VAT returns are filed periodically.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating without input VAT deduction loss applies to the export of goods to destinations outside Switzerland and to certain offshore services supplied to recipients abroad. The supplier must substantiate the physical export through customs documents and prove that the recipient is a foreign person or validly carrying out offshore activities. Film licensing royalties paid by foreign licensees generally qualify as exported services under the Swiss VAT Act if the recipient is outside Switzerland.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Bill of Lading, Airway Bill, or CMR transport document
Commercial invoice issued to foreign acquirer
Evidence of cross-border payment, such as SWIFT credit advice
Foreign acquirer VAT registration or business identity document where applicable
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Swiss tax and customs authorities may conduct retroactive audits and reassess zero-rated export supplies where documentation is deficient. Fraudulent claims for export zero-rating are subject to value-added tax clawback plus default interest at 4% per year, and penalties under Art. 82 and 83 of the Swiss VAT Act of up to four times the VAT evaded. In serious cases imprisonment is possible and controlling persons may be held primarily liable.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Swiss National Bank (SNB) / Schweizerische Nationalbank, governed by the National Bank Act 2003 and the Federal Act on Currency and Means of Payment; prudential conduct supervised by the Swiss Financial Market Supervisory Authority (FINMA).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: CHF is fully convertible with a free-floating regime; Switzerland imposes no capital controls and no separate exchange-control approval is required for current-account royalty flows or capital-account equity injections. Profit and royalty remittance from a Swiss AG is unrestricted at the FX/treasury layer; however, banks will require documentary evidence of the underlying licensing contract, beneficial ownership, and tax status because the 35% Swiss withholding tax on distributions is collected at source. Capital vs current account classification follows IMF BPM6; both are open, but high-value cash transactions above CHF 100,000 trigger AMLA identification duties.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. Swiss law mandates no statutory timeline, no mandatory conversion ratio, and no surrender obligation for export receipts or copyright royalty proceeds. Corporate exporters may hold foreign currency balances freely in any bank; reporting obligations are imposed only on banks for SNB balance-of-payments statistics (annual corporate registration with the SNB is required only when a Swiss resident is a lending/borrowing relationship exceeding CHF 10 million, which is not applicable to standard film licensing treasury).

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account + segregated Capital Escrow Account for licensing advances
Operational Account + dedicated royalty collection account

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Banque Cantonale Vaudoise (BCV, cantonal bank in Lausanne)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account with media/film industry desk facilities
Operational Account only (limited LC and cross-border trade finance capacity)
Operational Account (private-banking oriented, suboptimal for film-trade clearing)
Operational Account (retail payment rails only; no documentary credit issuance)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low-to-Medium. Swiss digital banks regulated as fintech licensees under FINMA (e.g., Yuh, Neon, SMNT) permit rapid remote onboarding and SEPA/SWIFT-adjacent transfers, but cannot issue or confirm Commercial Letters of Credit (UCP 600) and typically cap high-value treasury volumes. Non-Swiss EU EMIs may only operate via a FINMA-approved branch or Swiss outsourcing arrangement under the Banking Act Art. 1b and FinIA; therefore, an offshore EMI as sole treasury rail is legally insufficient for LC settlements and is contraindicated; use only as a supplementary collection conduit for micro-royalty receipts.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence is de facto mandatory for the UBOs and at least one managing director of a foreign-held AG at UBS, ZKB, and BCV; remote video identification is legally permissible under FINMA Circular 2016/07 only for Swiss-resident signatories with a Swiss ID, so non-resident directors must attend an in-person interview at the bank premises or at a Swiss consulate with an apostilled notarized mandate. Regarding the entity itself, the AG's incorporation documents, commercial register excerpt (Handelsregisterauszug), and certified signatures are required; the bank may also perform a recorded video call with the local registered agent as a supplementary control.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Underwriting red flag: Unclear chain of film copyright title or discrepancy between licensing territories and expected royalty counter-flows.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarized chain-of-title opinion from Swiss/IP counsel, registered copyright assignments with territorial schedules, production/distribution agreements, and a cash-flow forecast evidencing licensing advances versus residual royalty streams.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Underwriting red flag: UBO resides in a non-OECD or politically exposed (PEP) jurisdiction, raising source-of-funds concerns for capital injection.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Independent asset-and-wealth source statement, bank references from the originating institution, tax residency certificates, apostilled UBO declaration (Form A/Form I per Swiss AMLO-FINMA), and a Swiss notary deed for the share purchase.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Underwriting red flag: Opaque ownership structure or historical bearer-share legacy raising beneficial-ownership ambiguity (bearer shares have been abolished in Switzerland).
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Current commercial register excerpt evidencing registered shares per Art. 622 CO, registry of shareholders (Aktienbuch), declaration of economic intent, and legal opinion confirming compliance with the 2019 bearer-share conversion requirement.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Underwriting red flag: Payments routed to/from high-risk or sanctions-adjacent territories for sub-licensing of film rights.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Sanctions screening evidence (SECO, EU, OFAC lists), territorial exclusivity matrix, end-beneficiary and end-use declarations, and contractual warranties from downstream licensees binding them to Swiss export controls.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Underwriting red flag: Royalty valuation appears non-arm's-length or involves future 'bogus' licence fees without a commercial production.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Transfer pricing documentation (OECD-compliant, TP report by a Big-4 firm), market-comparable royalty benchmarks for the ISIC 5911 sector, and projected P&L from the entrusted film catalogue.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant routing for equity injection: SWIFT MT103 from the parent/shareholder with field 50K account details, field 72 narrative 'EQUITY CAPITAL INCREASE CH_AG - ZEICHNUNG AKTIENKAPITAL', and the ISO 20022 purpose code 'EQI' or 'CFDI' for capital payments into the bank's capital control assignment; the bank will verify the notarized capital increase resolution (Beurkundung), the updated commercial register excerpt, and the deposited share capital proof (Einzahlungsschein). Royalty/licence inflows must be labelled with purpose code 'ROYA' (royalties) or 'LICF' (licence fees) in field 77B/CTI of MT103, referencing the specific film licensing agreement and invoice number; inbound SEPA-equivalent instructions use the CH-NEMO ISO 20022 pain.001 message with the same purpose code. No SNB approval is required, but the bank will apply expedited sanctions screening and may ask for the underlying contract on first use.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Primary clearing rail: SWIFT MT103 for sub-licence payments, producer advances, and profit-participation remittances using purpose codes 'ROYA'/'LICF' and sequential payment identification. For secured transactions (minimum guarantee payments and delivery of film masters/promo materials against payment), use SWIFT MT700 (issuance) and MT707 (amendment) under UCP 600 Commercial Letters of Credit, confirmed by a first-class Swiss or European bank, with presentation of shipping/insurance documents, delivery certificates, and copyright warranty statements. Documentary collections under URC 522 (MT400/MT910) are a fallback for low-risk, same-bank relationships; domestic CHF/SEPA payments use the Swiss QR-bill (ISO 20022 QR-IBAN) rail, but this is inapplicable to cross-border film licensing.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable outright FX forwards (EUR/CHF, USD/CHF, GBP/CHF) with maturities matching royalty receipt dates, under an ISDA 2002 Master Agreement with a Swiss bank counterparty
FX swaps (swap legs) for staggered repatriation of minimum guarantees without disturbing the operational CHF liquidity buffer
Cross-currency interest rate swaps (CCIRS) under an ISDA/CSA with zero-threshold collateral in CHF for term-transforming film-finance advances
European vanilla FX options (call/put on USD/CHF or EUR/CHF) purchased as insurance on large licensing milestones; options writing is prohibited by bank policy

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) solely for hedging exposure to illiquid non-convertible currencies (e.g., certain emerging-market sub-licensing territories); NDFs on CHF are unnecessary and are not cleared via the SNB because the CHF is fully convertible

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate income tax return and annual financial statements (federal, cantonal and communal)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Cantonal Tax Office of registered office (e.g., Steueramt Zug) and Swiss Federal Tax Administration (ESTV)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months after the balance-sheet date; extension to eight months available on timely request in most cantons
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Default interest on outstanding tax, late-filing administrative penalties, official estimated assessment, and enforced collection; tax delinquency alone does not trigger automatic strike-off, but persistent insolvency can lead to bankruptcy and subsequent deletion from the Commercial Register.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual VAT return under yearly or quarterly filing scheme approved by ESTV
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Swiss Federal Tax Administration (ESTV), VAT Main Office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual scheme: within 60 days after the year-end; quarterly scheme: within 60 days after each quarter-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: VAT default interest, disallowance of input VAT deductions, administrative fines up to CHF 8,000, and criminal penalty proceedings for deliberate or negligent VAT evasion.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual employer wage declaration and AHV/IV/EO social-security contribution settlement
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Responsible compensation office (e.g., Zentralschweizer Ausgleichskasse or comparable cantonal clearing house)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual wage declaration and reconciliation due within the deadline set by the compensation office, normally by end of January or February of the following year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Default interest, late-payment surcharges, and administrative penalties for incorrect payroll reporting; directors may be personally liable for unpaid employer social-security contributions.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Ordinary audit is mandatory if an AG exceeds two of the following three thresholds in two consecutive years: balance sheet total CHF 20 million, revenue CHF 40 million, or annual average of 250 full-time employees. Listed companies and companies with outstanding bonds are always subject to ordinary audit. Other AGs require at least a limited audit unless all shareholders waive the audit and the company has ten or fewer full-time employees, in which case the audit may be dispensed with by shareholder resolution.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Swiss Code of Obligations (Art. 958 et seq.) accounting rules; Swiss GAAP FER is the local GAAP for annual accounts; IFRS is permitted for listed and internationally oriented companies.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Switzerland maintains no public UBO register. The AG must keep an up-to-date share register, and where a Swiss financial intermediary maintains accounts it must verify beneficial ownership continuously under AML rules. Annual UBO confirmation filing to a government body is not required. For an unlisted AG, transfer of registered shares requires written assignment and board approval, with the register updated promptly; significant shareholding changes are reported in the annual corporate tax return to the cantonal tax authorities.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Minute Book of general meetings and board resolutions
Commercial register excerpt and Articles of Association

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: CHF 2,000–6,000 per annum (approx. USD 2,300–7,000), depending on canton and service provider
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: CHF 5,000–20,000 per annum (approx. USD 5,800–23,000) when audit is required; in practice CHF 0 if a valid audit waiver applies

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 8.5% federal corporate income tax rate levied on post-tax profit (effective pre-tax equivalent approximately 7.83%); combined cantonal/communal rates vary by jurisdiction, producing an aggregate effective rate of approximately 12%–24% for most profit-active companies.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Cantonal tax privileges for holding, domicile, and mixed companies (phase-out completed under the 2020 Tax Reform and AHV Financing, TRAF); patent box regime allowing reduced taxation of qualifying IP income at cantonal level; additional R&D superdeduction of up to 150%; notional interest deduction on excess equity permitted in certain cantons; federal and cantonal tax holidays are available only in limited economically depressed zones and require authorization.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Annual corporate income tax return for legal entities (Formulaire pour personnes morales / Steuererklärung juristische Personen), filed with the competent cantonal tax administration. Electronic filing is available via the cantonal e-tax portals (e.g., SwissTax, EasyGov, or official cantonal e-filing systems). The federal tax assessment is integrated into the same cantonal return.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The tax return must be filed within six months after the end of the fiscal year; cantonal extensions are granted upon request, but the formal deadline cannot generally exceed 12 months after fiscal year-end. Interim payments of federal and cantonal corporate income tax are due quarterly based on prior assessments.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Identification of the company: legal entity name, registered seat, UID number (Unternehmens-Identifikationsnummer), and contact details.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident companies with a Swiss permanent establishment must enter the Swiss PE particulars and the foreign head office details, including the jurisdiction of tax residence.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Statement of net income before taxes, derived from the statutory annual financial statements prepared in accordance with Swiss GAAP or IFRS (or another permitted accounting standard).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident companies allocate net income attributable to the Swiss permanent establishment in accordance with the OECD authorised OECD approach (AOA); the PE’s separate accounting and capital attribution must be supported by transfer pricing documentation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Adjustments for non-deductible expenses and tax privileged income, including income from equity holdings (participation exemption), IP income eligible for patent box, and non-deductible royalty payments to non-arm's-length related parties.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident companies must adjust for costs recharged or profits attributed to the Swiss PE under arm's length principles and provide a TP documentation index if above the Swiss documentation thresholds.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable net profit after adjustments; presentation of state aid, tax credits, withholding tax credits, and any foreign tax credits claimed.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign tax credits for Swiss PE income are only available under DTA rules; the non-resident company must attach Form 823/824 and a tax residence certificate as applicable.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalties range from CHF 100 to CHF 10,000 per infraction, plus default interest on the assessed tax arrears (currently approximately 4%–5% per annum). Deliberate failure to file may lead to a penalty of up to 30% of the tax due and criminal prosecution for tax evasion.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 35% statutory Swiss federal withholding tax (Verrechnungssteuer) on gross dividends paid by a Swiss stock corporation (AG). Reduced rates may apply under Swiss double tax agreements (DTAs) up to the withholding tax cap in the relevant treaty; under the Switzerland-EU Savings Agreement, certain EU parent corporations may be eligible for a reduced 0% rate on dividends under the parent-subsidiary directive parity provision.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke DTA relief, the non-resident recipient must (i) be the beneficial owner of the dividend; (ii) provide a current tax residence certificate (Form 823) from its fiscal authority; (iii) submit Form 823 to the Swiss Federal Tax Administration (ESTV) before the payment to obtain an authorization for reduced-rate withholding, or alternatively file a refund claim with ESTV using Form 824 within three years after the payment; (iv) disclose any chain of intermediary entities to avoid treaty shopping; and (v) demonstrate substantive economic activity in the residence state if a preferential DTA rate is claimed.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory withholding: royalties paid by a Swiss resident for the use of intellectual property (including film licensing) are not subject to Swiss withholding tax; interest paid on ordinary commercial loans is not subject to Swiss withholding tax either. Swiss withholding tax applies only to dividends, interest from bonds, and interest from deposits with Swiss banks (35%). Treaty rates for royalties and debt interest generally range from 0% to 10%, depending on the applicable DTA and the presence of a genuine beneficial owner; film licensing royalties are typically classified as royalties under the OECD Model and protected by the DTA business profits or royalty article.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Local File must be prepared and submitted upon request by the tax authority if the annual gross revenue of the Swiss taxpayer exceeds CHF 10 million; Master File is required when the group’s consolidated annual revenue exceeds CHF 50 million. Country-by-Country reporting applies to Swiss-parented groups with consolidated group revenue of at least CHF 900 million and for Swiss subsidiaries of foreign groups with similar group thresholds. Transfer pricing documentation must be produced in German, French, or Italian (or accompanied by an official-certified translation into the tax authority's language).
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Switzerland does not operate a standalone Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) regime of the type found in the UAE or other tax havens. However, Swiss tax law and anti-abuse rules require a corporation to have actual economic substance, including a registered office at its declared Swiss seat, a valid VAT and employer registration (where applicable), physical business premises, business bank account, records, bookkeeping, and able directors with authority. DTA benefits are denied under the general anti-abuse rule (GAAR) and the OECD principal purpose test (PPT) where an arrangement was designed to obtain treaty benefits without genuine economic substance. The Swiss Federal Tax Administration may disregard a corporate structure or reclassify transactions as a permanent establishment if substance is insufficient.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Active tax evasion (Steuerhinterziehung) and fraudulent misrepresentation
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Submitting tax declarations with falsified accounts, deliberately understating taxable revenue from film licensing distributions, fabricating expense invoices, or concealing Swiss-source income or assets in foreign accounts.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Fine of up to three times the amount of evaded tax, plus default interest and the full back-tax assessment for up to ten years (longer in cases of fraud). In aggravated cases involving fraudulent conduct, the tax administration may order criminal prosecution before cantonal courts.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and officers who sign or are otherwise complicit in false declarations can be personally liable for the tax arrears and fines; the criminal penalty may include imprisonment for up to three years (up to ten years for repeat or large-scale fraud) and travel bans may be imposed by the cantonal tax authority.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer pricing mispricing and documentary default
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Charging non-arm's-length royalty rates on film licensing agreements, unreported year-end adjustments, lack of contemporaneous transfer pricing documentation, or failure to maintain functional and risk analyses for the Swiss licensing entity.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Praxis adjustment by the tax authority increasing taxable income by the arm's-length price differential, assessment of 5% late-payment interest on the additional tax, and penalties for incomplete or late disclosure of transfer pricing documentation, generally up to CHF 10,000 per violation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be held personally liable for the additional Swiss tax and penalties if they intentionally instructed or approved the mispricing, had knowledge of the deficiency, and failed to take corrective measures. Swiss insolvency law provides for creditor clawback claims against directors where corporate assets were depleted by unlawful transactions.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: A Swiss AG formed solely for tax treaty or withholding tax advantages with no real office, no employees, no business activity, no own bank account, or whose directors are nominees with no decision-making authority, especially when combined with a letter-box operation receiving film license royalties.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Denial of DTA relief, requalification of income as distributed to the ultimate beneficial owner, and reinstatement of 35% Swiss withholding tax on the undeclared distribution. The tax authority may also reassess the company as a managed or foreign-controlled permanent establishment and apply Swiss tax on the entire net base.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Nominee directors can be held jointly and severally liable for unpaid withheld tax and company tax debts under Swiss tax debt liability rules (Art. 12 ff. Federal Act on the Collection of Taxes). Directors who knowingly maintained a sham company may be subject to criminal penalties for aiding and abetting tax evasion, including fines and imprisonment, and may be prohibited from managing Swiss entities by the commercial registry in cases of repeated non-compliance.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Non-collection and non-remittance of Swiss withholding tax
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to withhold 35% Swiss federal withholding tax on dividends, or on interest from bonds and bank deposits, and failure to remit the withheld tax to the Swiss Federal Tax Administration within the statutory deadline.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The company is liable for the full 35% withholding tax on gross payments, plus default interest of 5% per annum. Willful failure to remit WHT constitutes a criminal offense under Art. 186 ff. of the Federal Direct Tax Act, with a fine of up to CHF 500,000 and, in aggravated cases, imprisonment.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are personally liable for the unremitted withholding tax if they were knowingly involved in the decision and the company is unable to pay. Swiss criminal law provision for tax offenses allows fines against directors acting in the corporate interest, and travel restrictions may be imposed pending criminal investigation.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating a film licensing company with anonymous beneficial ownership, using opaque private letters of credit or SWIFT wires from tax havens, or failing to identify the film copyright seller and ultimate royalty beneficiary in jurisdictions with high AML risk.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the Swiss Anti-Money Laundering Act (AMLA), financial intermediaries and companies carrying out commercial transactions in cash of over CHF 100,000 have reporting obligations; violations are punishable with fines up to CHF 500,000. If the film licence income is traceable to tax evasion or corruption, the assets can be frozen and confiscated under the Swiss Criminal Code proficiency law.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be prosecuted under the Swiss Criminal Code for failing to conduct the required identification of beneficial owners, failure to report suspicious transaction reports to the Money Laundering Reporting Office Switzerland (MROS), and for participating in a criminal organisation; personal sanctions include imprisonment of up to five years, seizure of personal assets, and permanent exclusion from serving as a company director.
